title: Chapter 6. Kirtanas and Gaura's Form in Navadvipa, the Lord's Ecstasy, Nityananda, Separation, and Nilachala
html:
Padas of contemporaries known from the *Padakalpataru (PK), the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR) and the Kshanada-gita-chintamani (KGC), in the order of the lilas: the Navadvipa kirtana through the eyes of Vasu Ramananda; praise of the Gaura-avatara (Narahari, Yadunatha Dasa); Gaura's form (Shankara Ghosha, Vasudeva Datta, Ramananda); the kirtana festival in Advaita's house (Vamshivadana); the Lord's dance in kirtana (Chaitanyadasa, Narahari, Ramananda); the Lord's ecstatic moods (Yadunatha Dasa, Vamshidasa); pastimes on the Ganga — the boat and the swing (Ramananda); Nityananda's dance in Srivasa's courtyard (Shankara Ghosha); Navadvipa after the sannyasa (Murari, Madhavi Dasa); kirtana and the festival of colours in Nilachala (Ramananda, Madhavi Dasa); and the poet's prayer (Ramananda). The text follows PK, BR, KGC and the Gaura-pada-tarangini (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

1. Vasu Ramananda — "caudige gobinda-dhvani śuni pahum̐ hāse…" (BR, p. 952; KGC 29.1)

Lila: a kirtana in Navadvipa: on every side the cry "Govinda!" resounds; the Lord laughs and dances together with Nityananda; Govinda, Madhava and Vasu (the Ghosha brothers) and Mukunda sing. Narahari Chakravarti cites the pada in the *Bhakti-ratnakara among the testimonies to the Navadvipa kirtanas. According to Majumdar it is the pada of an eyewitness of the Navadvipa kirtana (1509); from the order of the names "Govinda — Madhava — Vasu" he infers that Govinda Ghosha was the eldest. Raga dhanashi (BR), mangala (KGC, GPT).*1

চৌদিগে গোবিন্দধ্বনি শুনি পহুঁ হাসে ।
কম্পিত অধরে গোরা গদ গদ ভাষে ॥

caudige gobindadhvani śuni pahum̐ hāse |
kampita adhare gorā gada gada bhāṣe ||

caudige — on every side; gobinda-dhvani — the cry "Govinda!"; śuni — hearing; pahum̐ hāse — the Lord laughs; kampita adhare — with trembling lips; gorā — Gora (Gaura); gada gada bhāṣe — speaks falteringly

1.1On every side — "Govinda!"; hearing it, the Lord laughs;
with trembling lips Gora speaks in a faltering voice.2

নাচয়ে গৌরাঙ্গ যার সঙ্গে নিত্যানন্দ ।
অবনী ভাসল প্রেমে বাঢ়ল আনন্দ ॥

nācaye gaurāṅga yāra saṅge nityānanda |
abanī bhāsala preme bāṛhala ānanda ||

nācaye gaurāṅga — Gauranga dances; yāra saṅge nityānanda — with whom [dances] Nityananda; abanī bhāsala preme — the earth is flooded with prema; bāṛhala ānanda — bliss swelled

1.2Gauranga dances, and with Him Nityananda;
the earth is flooded with prema, and bliss has swelled.

গোবিন্দ মাধব বাসু গায়েন মুকুন্দ ।
ভুলিল কীর্তনরসে পায়া নিজবৃন্দ ॥

gobinda mādhaba bāsu gāyena mukunda |
bhulila kīrtanarase pāyā nijabṛnda ||

gobinda mādhaba bāsu — Govinda, Madhava, Vasu (the Ghosha brothers); gāyena mukunda — and Mukunda sings; bhulila — He forgot [Himself]; kīrtana-rase — in the taste of kirtana; pāyā (= pāiyā) nija-bṛnda — having found His own (companions)

1.3Govinda, Madhava, Vasu and Mukunda sing;
having found His own, He forgot Himself in the taste of kirtana.3

রঙ্গিয়া সঙ্গিয়া সে অমিয়া-রসে ভোর ।
বসু রামানন্দ তাহে লুবধ চকোর ॥

raṅgiyā saṅgiyā se amiyā-rase bhora |
basu rāmānanda tāhe lubadha cakora ||

raṅgiyā — joyful; saṅgiyā — companions; se amiyā-rase bhora — are drunk with the nectarean taste; basu rāmānanda — Vasu Ramananda; tāhe — in this; lubadha cakora — a thirsting chakora

1.4The joyful companions are drunk with the nectarean taste,
and Vasu Ramananda in this is a thirsting chakora.4

same), 1960 ed. vv. 3426–3429, 2006 ed. vv. 3426–3429; in BR the pada stands in a series of padas on the Navadvipa kirtana, near the pada of Chaitanyadasa (below, no. 10). A second recension: KGC, 29th kshanada (shukla-chaturdashi), no. 1 (pp. 229–230, raga mangala); GPT1 — p. 270, no. 73 (Majumdar's "p. 27" is evidently a misprint); GPT2 — sect. 4.2, no. 73. In it the first and the last half-lines agree, but the middle differs (see note 3 and VAR); Majumdar considered the GPT text corrupt. The pada is not in PK. Majumdar: Vasu Ramananda of Kulinagrama, a descendant of Maladhara Vasu, was a contemporary of the Lord (CC Madhya 15). Ghosha. Gora is Gaura. "Trembling lips… faltering voice" are signs of ecstasy (sattvika-bhavas). Gauranga dances, and with Him Nityananda; the earth is flooded with prema, Ramananda sings. To Mukunda, Murari, Vasu He says: 'Come here!' — for your virtues the Darling of [our] life weeps" (GPT: "Murari, Mukunda, come…"); and instead of the first line of 1.4: "All the other devotees are drunk with bliss". The double mention of Ramananda (in 1.2 and in the signature) argues for the BR recension. moonlike face.

2. Narahari — "anupāma gorā-abatāra…" (PK 2288)

Praise of the Gaura-avatara: the Lord spread through all lands the taste of ninefold bhakti, making no distinction of caste; in the age of Kali, where people sin, the holy name easily carries them across — what in other ages was attained with great toil through sacrifice, japa, meditation and worship. In PK it stands in the 21st pallava, next to padas on Gaura the sannyasi. Raga varadi.5

অনুপাম গোরা-অবতার ।
নবধা ভকতি-রস বিস্তারিলা সব দেশ
না করিলা জাতির বিচার ॥ ধ্রু ॥

anupāma gorā-abatāra |
nabadhā bhakati-rasa bistārilā saba deśa
nā karilā jātira bicāra || dhru ||

anupāma — peerless; gorā-abatāra — the descent of Gora; nabadhā bhakati-rasa — the taste of ninefold bhakti; bistārilā saba deśa — He spread through all lands; nā karilā jātira bicāra — made no distinction of caste

2.1(Refrain) Peerless is the descent of Gora!
The taste of ninefold bhakti He spread through all lands,
making no distinction of caste.6

এমন ঠাকুর ভজ দূর কর সব কাজ
ছাড় সব মিছা অভিলাষ ।
চৈতন্যচাঁদের গুণে আলো কৈল ত্রিভুবনে
অনায়াসে হৈল পরকাশ ॥

emana ṭhākura bhaja dūra kara saba kāja
chāṛa saba michā abhilāṣa |
caitanyacām̐dera guṇe ālo kaila tribhubane
anāyāse haila parakāśa ||

emana ṭhākura bhaja — worship such a Lord; dūra kara saba kāja — cast aside all concerns; chāṛa saba michā abhilāṣa — give up all false desires; caitanya-cām̐dera guṇe — by the virtues of Chaitanyachand; ālo kaila tribhubane — the three worlds were lit; anāyāse haila parakāśa — effortlessly He was manifest

2.2Worship such a Lord, cast aside all [other] concerns,
give up all false desires.
By the virtues of Chaitanyachand the three worlds are lit —
effortlessly He revealed Himself.

চৈতন্য-কলপতরু অখিল-জীবের গুরু
গোলোক-বৈভব সব সঙ্গে ।
জীবেরে মলিন দেখি হৈয়া সকরুণ-আঁখি
হরি-নাম বিলাইল রঙ্গে ॥

caitanya-kalapataru akhila-jībera guru
goloka-baibhaba saba saṅge |
jībere malina dekhi haiyā sakaruṇa-ām̐khi
hari-nāma bilāila raṅge ||

caitanya-kalapataru — Chaitanya, the wish-fulfilling tree; akhila-jībera guru — the guru of all beings; goloka-baibhaba saba saṅge — all the splendour of Goloka with Him; jībere malina dekhi — seeing the beings defiled; haiyā sakaruṇa-ām̐khi — with compassionate eyes; hari-nāma bilāila raṅge — joyfully gave out the name of Hari

2.3Chaitanya is a wish-fulfilling tree, the guru of all living beings;
with Him is all the splendour of Goloka.
Seeing the living beings defiled, with compassionate eyes
He joyfully gave out the name of Hari.

যজ্ঞ জপ ধ্যান পূজা অন্য যুগে যত প্রজা
সাধিলেক অতি বড় দুখে ।
এই যে কলি-যুগ-নরে যত পাপ তাই করে
নাম লৈয়া তরি গেল সুখে ॥

yajña japa dhyāna pūjā anya yuge yata prajā
sādhileka ati baṛa dukhe |
ei ye kali-yuga-nare yata pāpa tāi kare
nāma laiyā tari gela sukhe ||

yajña japa dhyāna pūjā — sacrifice, japa, meditation, worship; anya yuge yata prajā — all the people of other ages; sādhileka ati baṛa dukhe — accomplished with very great toil; ei ye kali-yuga-nare — these people of the Kali age; yata pāpa tāi kare — however much sin they commit; nāma laiyā tari gela sukhe — taking the name, crossed over with ease

2.4Sacrifice, japa, meditation, worship — all that people did in other ages
they accomplished with very great toil.
But these people of the age of Kali, however much they sin —
taking the name, they crossed over with ease.7

করুণা-বিগ্রহ সার তুলনা কি দিব আর
পতিতের পূরাইল আশ ।
কিছু না বুঝিয়া চিতে কান্দিয়া কান্দিয়া পথে
গুণ গায় নরহরি দাস ॥

karuṇā-bigraha sāra tulanā ki diba āra
patitera pūrāila āśa |
kichu nā bujhiyā cite kāndiyā kāndiyā pathe
guṇa gāya narahari dāsa ||

karuṇā-bigraha sāra — the essence, compassion embodied; tulanā ki diba āra — with whom else can He be compared?; patitera pūrāila āśa — fulfilled the hopes of the fallen; kichu nā bujhiyā cite — understanding nothing in his heart; kāndiyā kāndiyā pathe — weeping and weeping on the road; guṇa gāya narahari dāsa — Narahari Dasa sings [His] virtues

2.5He is the essence, compassion embodied; with whom else can He be compared?
He fulfilled the hopes of the fallen.
Understanding nothing in his heart, weeping and weeping on the road,
Narahari Dasa sings His virtues.8

varadi; MS P-R-Sa no. 2392. GPT1 — p. 28, no. 5 (raga varadi); GPT2 — sect. 1.3, no. 5. In Ray's index of poets it is among the padas of Narahari. Majumdar does not discuss this pada; its simple Bengali without heaped ornament fits his criteria for the genuine padas of Narahari Sarakara, but the attribution (Sarakara or Narahari Chakravarti) is unproven. — cf. CC Adi 7 on the distribution of prema to all without discrimination. GPT: "spreading [it] with the taste of bhakti through all lands, He made no distinction of caste". attained in Kali-yuga by chanting the name of Hari. GPT1 in 2.4: "but in this darkness of Kali, however much people sin — taking the name, they cross over with ease". he sings. MS P-R-Sa: "weeping, weeping"; "with whom can He be compared" (tāra for āra).

3. Narahari (?) — "pāsarā nā yāya āmāra gorācām̐dera līlā…" (PK 2344)

Praise of Gaura: the pastimes of Gorachand cannot be forgotten — by His virtues beasts and birds weep and stones melt; the name inaccessible to Brahma He gave out to the three worlds. In PK the pada has no signature (its last line speaks of Nityananda); in GPT it bears the signature of Narahari Dasa. In PK it stands in the 25th pallava ("Description of the form and virtues of Sri Chaitanya and Nityananda"). Raga vibhasa.9

পাসরা না যায় আমার গোরাচাঁদের লীলা ।
যাহার গুণে পশুপাখী ঝুরে সদা দুটি আঁখি
গলিয়া গলিয়া পড়ে শিলা ॥ ধ্রু ॥

pāsarā nā yāya āmāra gorācām̐dera līlā |
yāhāra guṇe paśupākhī jhure sadā duṭi ām̐khi
galiyā galiyā paṛe śilā || dhru ||

pāsarā nā yāya — cannot be forgotten; āmāra gorācām̐dera līlā — the pastimes of my Gorachand; yāhāra guṇe — by whose virtues; paśu-pākhī — beasts and birds; jhure sadā duṭi ām̐khi — ever weep from both eyes; galiyā galiyā paṛe śilā — stones melt and melt

3.1(Refrain) I cannot forget the pastimes of my Gorachand!
By His virtues beasts and birds ever weep from both eyes,
and stones melt and melt.

যাহার নামের লাগি মহেশ হইলা যোগী
বিরিঞ্চি ভাবয়ে অনুক্ষণে ।
ব্রহ্মার দুর্লভ নাম সুলভ করিয়া পহু
যাচিয়া দেয়ল ত্রিভুবনে ॥

yāhāra nāmera lāgi maheśa hailā yogī
biriñci bhābaye anukṣaṇe |
brahmāra durlabha nāma sulabha kariyā pahu
yāciyā deyala tribhubane ||

yāhāra nāmera lāgi — for the sake of whose name; maheśa hailā yogī — Mahesha (Shiva) became a yogi; biriñci bhābaye anukṣaṇe — Virinchi (Brahma) meditates incessantly; brahmāra durlabha nāma — the name hard for Brahma to obtain; sulabha kariyā pahum̐ — the Lord, making it easy to obtain; yāciyā deyala tribhubane — entreating, gave it to the three worlds

3.2For the sake of His name Mahesha became a yogi,
Virinchi meditates [on Him] incessantly.
The name inaccessible even to Brahma the Lord made easy to obtain —
and Himself, entreating, gave it to the three worlds.10

গৌরাঙ্গ-অঙ্গ শোভে পুলক-কদম্ব তাহে
অপরূপ শ্রীঅঙ্গের শোভা ।
আনন্দে বিভোর ঠাকুর নিত্যানন্দ
দেখিয়া কনকের আভা ॥

gaurāṅga-aṅga śobhe pulaka-kadamba tāhe
aparūpa śrīaṅgera śobhā |
ānande bibhora ṭhākura nityānanda
dekhiyā kanakera ābhā ||

gaurāṅga-aṅga śobhe — Gauranga's body shines; pulaka-kadamba tāhe — on it hair standing on end like kadamba blossoms; aparūpa śrī-aṅgera śobhā — wondrous the beauty of the holy body; ānande bibhora — lost in bliss; ṭhākura nityānanda — Thakura Nityananda; dekhiyā kanakera ābhā — seeing the golden radiance

3.3Gauranga's body shines, and on it the hair stands on end like kadamba blossoms:
wondrous is the beauty of His holy body!
In bliss Thakura Nityananda is lost to Himself,
seeing that golden radiance.11

vibhasa; MS P-R-Sa no. 2448. There is no signature in PK. GPT1 — p. 28, no. 7, and GPT2 — sect. 1.3, no. 7 (both raga vibhasa) give the last line with a signature: "In bliss Narahari Dasa is lost to himself, seeing that golden radiance". The PK line is shorter than the tripadi metre requires (one member is missing), while the GPT line fits it; perhaps PK preserved a line in which the poet's name was lost. The attribution to Narahari (still less to Sarakara) is unproven. asked (cf. CC Adi 3). ("ka").

4. Yadunatha Dasa — "aparūpa cām̐da udaya nadiyāpure…" (PK 2191)

Praise of Gaura: a wondrous Moon has risen in Nadia, and darkness has left the three worlds; the Lord whom Shesha, Shankara, Narada and Brahma praise rolls on the ground in bliss on hearing His own virtues; from His eyes flows an ocean of the nectar of prema. According to M-1961 it is a pada of Yadunatha Dasa (Kavichandra), a fellow countryman of Jagannatha Mishra and a contemporary of the Lord. Raga dhanashi.12

অপরূপ চাঁদ উদয় নদিয়াপুরে
তিমির নাহি রে ত্রিভুবনে ।
অবনিতে অখিল জিবের শোক নাশল
নিগম-নিগূঢ় প্রেম-দানে ॥

aparūpa cām̐da udaya nadiyāpure
timira nāhi re tribhubane |
abanite akhila jibera śoka nāśala
nigama-nigūṛha prema-dāne ||

aparūpa cām̐da — a wondrous moon; udaya nadiyāpure — has risen in the town of Nadia; timira nāhi re tribhubane — there is no darkness in the three worlds; abanite — on earth; akhila jibera śoka nāśala — destroyed the sorrow of all beings; nigama-nigūṛha prema-dāne — by giving the prema hidden in the Vedas

4.1A wondrous Moon has risen in the town of Nadia —
there is no more darkness in the three worlds!
On earth He destroyed the sorrow of all living beings,
bestowing the prema hidden in the Vedas.

আরে মোর গৌরাঙ্গসুন্দর রায় ।
ভকত-হৃদয়-কুমুদ পরকাশল
অকিঞ্চন-জিবের উপায় ॥

āre mora gaurāṅgasundara rāya |
bhakata-hṛdaya-kumuda parakāśala
akiñcana-jibera upāya ||

āre mora gaurāṅgasundara rāya — O my Gaurangasundara Raya; bhakata-hṛdaya-kumuda parakāśala — made the lilies of the devotees' hearts unfold; akiñcana-jibera upāya — the salvation of the destitute

4.2(Refrain) O my Gaurangasundara Raya!
He made the lilies of the devotees' hearts unfold —
the salvation of the destitute.13

শেষ শঙ্কর নারদ চতুরানন
নিরবধি যার গুণ গায় ।
সো পহু নিরুপম নিজ-গুণ শুনইতে
আনন্দে ধরণী লোটায় ॥

śeṣa śaṅkara nārada caturānana
nirabadhi yāra guṇa gāya |
so pahu nirupama nija-guṇa śunaite
ānande dharaṇī loṭāya ||

śeṣa śaṅkara nārada caturānana — Shesha, Shankara, Narada, the Four-faced; nirabadhi yāra guṇa gāya — incessantly sing whose virtues; so pahu nirupama — that incomparable Lord; nija-guṇa śunaite — hearing His own virtues; ānande dharaṇī loṭāya — rolls on the ground in bliss

4.3Shesha, Shankara, Narada, the Four-faced One
incessantly sing His virtues;
and this incomparable Lord, hearing His own virtues,
rolls on the ground in bliss.14

অরুণ নয়ানে বরুণ-আলয়
বহয়ে প্রেম-সুধা-জল ।
যদুনাথ দাস বলে যেন সোণার কমলে
প্রসবিছে মুকুতার ফল ॥

aruṇa nayāne baruṇa-ālaya
bahaye prema-sudhā-jala |
yadunātha dāsa bale yena soṇāra kamale
prasabiche mukutāra phala ||

aruṇa nayāne — from the reddish eyes; baruṇa-ālaya — an ocean (abode of Varuna); bahaye prema-sudhā-jala — flows the nectar-water of prema; yadunātha dāsa bale — Yadunatha Dasa says; yena soṇāra kamale — as if a golden lotus; prasabiche mukutāra phala — were bearing pearls

4.4From His reddish eyes there flows, [like] an ocean,
the nectarean water of prema.
Yadunatha Dasa says: it is as if from a golden lotus
pearls were being born.15

P-R-Sa no. 2299. GPT1 — p. 35, no. 27 (raga dhanashi); GPT2 — sect. 1.3 (OCR 18989). Yadunatha Kavichandra was the youngest son of Ratnagarbha Acharya, a fellow countryman and friend of Jagannatha Mishra (CB Adi 2; CC Adi 11 — in the branch of Nityananda); B. B. Majumdar (Padas of the Sixteenth Century, 1961) considers him a contemporary who wrote of Gaura's moods as an eyewitness, and distinguishes him from Yadunandana. Cf. his padas below (nos. 14–15). (akiñcana) — those who have nothing but devotion. Name" instead of "Narada". Cf. Bhag. 10.14 (Brahma's praise). tears on Gaura's golden face are pearls "born" of a golden lotus. GPT1: "Yadunatha Dasa says: by the [good] fortune (lit. the fruit of karma) of the living beings He brings forth these pearls".

5. Shankara Ghosha — "dekha dekha sundara śacī-nandanā…" (KGC 24.1)

Gaura's form in Navadvipa: arms reaching to the knees, the gait of an intoxicated elephant, a garland of malati, a face lovelier than the autumn moon, eyes full of the tears of prema's bliss; with His companions He ceaselessly plays and sings "Hari, Hari". According to M-1961 it is a pada of Shankara Ghosha, a mridanga player and a contemporary of the Navadvipa period. Raga beloyar.16

দেখ দেখ সুন্দর শচী-নন্দনা ।
আজানুলম্বিত ভুজ বাহু সুবলনা ॥

dekha dekha sundara śacī-nandanā |
ājānulambita bhuja bāhu subalanā ||
